scope: Static coordinate reading, supplied-formula and isolated arithmetic checks; no driving claim or preset promotion.

protocol.representation_contract: Named adds only an exact raw copy of the existing 15 m x/y values to full state. Isolated arithmetic provides only those raw x/y values as a separate task.

interpretation: All 96 separate full-state readback answers are correct. This rules out a universal inability to locate/read the displayed pair on these cases, not faulty extraction within separately asked formula questions.

The 24 wrong denominator answers comprise 15 x*x+y and 9 225+y*y distractors. None is x+y or an arbitrary fallback. Their minimum absolute numeric error is about 0.164 square metres, over 300 times the 0.0005 rounding half-unit; these are substantive expression alternatives rather than three-decimal rounding disagreements.

With a correct numerator and the selected wrong denominator, only 8 of 24 wrong component answers would change the coarse supplied-rule wheel label; 16 preserve it. This hypothetical offline calculation is not a selected control and does not identify how the model obtained separate formula answers.

Nonzero formula choices follow raw-y sign on 44/48 table-atan choices and on all 46 named-atan,30 table-bin and36 named-bin choices. The four exceptions are mirrored straight-target cases where table-atan selected moderate steering with current-road-heading sign. This weakens a universal heading-sign shortcut but does not prove arithmetic execution.
Target magnitude composition differs between heading-mismatch groups; compare the nonstraight subgroup before attributing aggregate score changes to sign conflicts.

A bounded fresh static question using substituted numeric literals could test expression-variable binding and squaring salience. Keep calculations and targets out of state, retain denominator and full-rule tasks separately, and avoid interpreting a combined expression rewrite as one isolated cognitive cause.
additional_limitations: All six nonstraight heading-sign-mismatch geometries have moderate targets. Heading mismatch and target magnitude are not independently crossed.

The isolated denominator was wrong on all 16 moderate-target component calls, yet both atan profiles were correct on all 16 corresponding formula calls. It was correct on 13/16 full-target components despite weak full-target formula performance. Separate task scores do not establish that denominator errors caused formula or driving errors.

limitations: Twenty-four synthetic geometries in twelve mirrored pairs and repeated conditions are not independent driving trials.
Named coordinates duplicate raw values already present in the full table; they add salience without supplying a target angle or recommended control.
Readback and formula answers come from separate questions. Correct readback does not prove the same extraction occurred inside a formula answer.
Isolated component questions use only x/y. Their contrast with full-state formula questions changes both context and task complexity, so it does not isolate a single cause.
The ratio thresholds are decimal approximations. They agree with the exact atan quantizer on every margin-protected fixture; exact boundary behavior is untested.
Coarse wheel answers generally cannot identify exact trigonometric execution. A supplied policy's label is not an optimal driving action.
Endpoint errors count as incorrect in attempted accuracy; planned coverage and unrun cases remain separate.

continuation.scope: Separate static denominator and supplied-rule question comparisons; no automatic driving trial or preset promotion.
